migration.description: Add archive identity proofs, a resumable bounded usage-breakdown repair cursor with deferred candidates, and generation-safe prompt-cache statistics publication.
migration.release_unit_description: Incremental maintenance repair and prompt-cache publication fencing.

durable_state.description: Archive replay SHA identities, ordered usage-breakdown repair progress with deferred candidates, and prompt-cache staging generation fences.
durable_state.storage_implementation: Additive main-database SQLite columns, replay identity and ordered repair-candidate indexes, a repair-progress table, and a deferred archive-repair queue with its ordering index. No public API fields or response status values change.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: v4.3.0 origin/main schema at 1f3881075b1fe749e964dda3ec66ab10b710c797 (post-Proxy #1096 merge); additive objects are readable by the same-Major schema initializer.
source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Candidate branch th/pr-maintenance-incremental; final commit and PR identity are bound by the delivery record.

public_api.description: No public HTTP or task-response contract changes; existing fields and status values remain unchanged.

database_migration.structural_change_assessment: All changes are additive and idempotent. Existing replay rows remain unverified until a current manifest SHA is explicitly written; no historical aggregate is fabricated by schema installation.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Ensure hourly_rollup_archive_replay.archive_sha256 exists and install the dataset/file/SHA lookup index. Existing legacy rows remain NULL or blank and are not promoted by DDL.

Create hourly_rollup_archive_repair_progress and add cursor_stale_rank, cursor_month_key, and cursor_created_at to an existing table when absent. The cursor key is initialized to the empty/default position and is installed before repair reads it.
Add nullable prompt_cache_conversation_stats_refresh_staging.pending_generation when absent. Existing staging accumulators retain their current generation and cursor values.

Install the ordered archive-batch repair-candidate indexes and create hourly_rollup_archive_repair_deferred with its per-scope retry ordering index. Deferred candidates preserve budget-exhausted work while the main cursor advances to later candidates.

dml_changes.description: Write replay markers with the completed manifest SHA; upstream-account marker repair fills only absent target rows and preserves stale or unknown markers, while usage-breakdown repair treats stale identities as full-rebuild work.

Advance the ordered repair cursor in the same transaction as each candidate decision; the shared elapsed budget gates selection of the next candidate while a selected candidate completes its validation and overlap closure as one transaction; retain and retry explicitly budget-interrupted deferred candidates without starving later recoverable rows, roll back safely on interruption, reset only after the ordered set is exhausted, and continue a bounded number of pages during bootstrap; pending cursor or deferred work defers the runtime task for a cancellation-aware retry.
Record pending_generation before discarding a page whose source generation changed, and publish only when the generation fence still matches. A stopped release is repaired forward by the next run.

historical_data_backfill_or_transformati.description: No readiness-wide historical scan is performed. Existing materialized archives are revisited only through bounded repair pages; the shared per-page elapsed budget gates candidate selection, while the selected archive validation and overlap closure may exceed that boundary and commit as one durable transaction, reusing source-bound temporary copies across cancellation and retry; unverified legacy markers remain quarantined until a verified replay.

progress_signals: Replay marker SHA equality with the current archive manifest
Durable repair cursor stale rank, month, creation time and archive id
Deferred archive-repair queue count, oldest deferred candidate, and retry outcome
Prompt-cache staging pending_generation and generation outcome
Committed candidate/page counts and deferred unreadable archives
pause_points: After idempotent schema installation and before background repair
After each committed archive repair candidate transaction
Before prompt-cache page publication when the source generation changes

recovery.program_rollback_state_behavior: An older same-Major binary may open additive SQLite objects but does not understand the new cursor or generation-fence protocol; rollback does not down-migrate or erase durable evidence.
recovery.faulty_release_recovery: A newer binary recognizes missing, stale, or pending identities, preserves last-good rollups when an archive is unreadable, and resumes the durable repair or staging state from its last committed boundary.

required_test_evidence: Repeated schema installation creates or upgrades replay identity, repair-candidate indexes, repair cursor, deferred queue, and pending-generation structures without changing legacy unverified marker values; the candidate query plan uses the ordered partial index.
A file-backed restart preserves the repair cursor and a stopped prompt-cache generation cannot publish a stale page.
A corrupted or unreadable archive leaves its materialized timestamp, replay marker, and last-good rollup rows intact.
A closure larger than one archive query page converges, and a deferred candidate does not starve a later recoverable candidate.
Current candidate Linux backend profiles and the required source-quality checks pass on the pushed commit.
